findings.F1: The effect sits in the deepest closes only. In folds B and C, on choppy up days, the deepest fifth of depth had a 5-day unusual move of -7.27 % (winsorised, 26 cases), against +0.21 % for the other four fifths (Welch t -2.82). The four shallower fifths gave -2.4 %, -1.2 %, -0.2 % and +9.2 %, with no steady gradient between them. A linear slope on the whole forecast therefore dilutes the effect, and step 5's slope t is only 0.94, on 841 cases.
findings.F2: The same shape shows the next day. On choppy up days, the deepest fifth fell -1.48 % beyond drift over one day (t -3.42, 153 cases), against -0.24 % for the rest (Welch t -2.72). The linear slope at 1 day has t 1.49 only, on 1,029 cases.
findings.F3: The linear slope is pulled about by single extreme moves in the shallow fifths. One DOGE case in w11, in the shallowest fifth, rose +384 % over 5 days, and that fifth's standard deviation is 0.53 against about 0.06 to 0.13 elsewhere. Winsorising at 1 % and 99 % moves the 5-day up-day slope t in folds B and C from 2.14 to 2.41, and the rank correlation is 0.17 (p 0.02, 184 cases).
findings.F4: The deep-close fall is not confined to a few periods. The deepest fifth's 5-day unusual move is negative in 9 of 12 windows (w7 to w18), with the largest in w16 (-30 %, 6 cases), and it holds on down days too (-5.5 % against -1.5 %, Welch t -1.82). The effect is the depth, read in its strongest cases, as the brief claims.
findings.F5: The idea's size is real but small against the market's drift. The unusual move is +0.78 % per case over 5 days (t 2.18, 936 days, strength 0.068), which is 3.5 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. But the coins' normal drift is -0.80 % in the short direction, so the total move per case is -0.03 %, and the book's Sharpe is -0.03.

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, on a day that closed up, the further the close sits below the coin's 20-day high, in units of its 20-day daily-return standard deviation, the larger its fall over the next five days. The fall grows faster than the depth, so the closes deepest below the high carry most of it.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorting up-day bounces in a sideways market should keep the short for the bounces that sit far below the recent high, and size it much more heavily as the depth grows, rather than in proportion to it.
ideas.name: deepest up-day five-day fade
